scenario_name: Courier says delivered, agent system says not yet shipped
judge_summary: The assistant handled the delivery-status issue competently, keeping details straight and giving the user a clear, actionable plan to resolve the discrepancy with Swiss Post and then escalate with Acme. It responded well to follow-up questions and confusion, refining its explanation until the user was satisfied. The only notable limitation was some lack of specificity about the ultimate outcome Acme would offer after escalation, though this caution avoided overpromising.

bot: Hello! What can I assist you with today?

transcript.user: Hi, I’d like to check the status of my Galaxy Watch order, please.
bot: Right, let me check that order status.

Your **Samsung Galaxy Watch 7** order (**ORD-20260628-001**, placed **June 28, 2026**) is currently **OPEN** and **being prepared for shipment** at the distribution center. It’s预计 to **ship July 1, 2026** with an **estimated delivery of July 3–5, 2026** via **Standard Post (Swiss Post)**, and **tracking isn’t available yet** (it will be assigned once it ships).

transcript.user: That’s odd, I just got an SMS from the courier saying the parcel was delivered today, but I don’t have anything. So where is it really?
bot: I’m sorry about that—let me check the latest tracking details.

In our system, the Galaxy Watch order **ORD-20260628-001** is still **being prepared for shipment** and **has not been assigned a tracking number yet**, so we don’t show it as shipped or delivered. That means I can’t confirm any “delivered” scan from here—your SMS may be for a different parcel or an attempted/misdirected delivery.

To narrow it down, does the SMS include a **tracking number** (or a link)? If you paste just the tracking number or courier name, I can compare it to what we have on the order.

transcript.user: Yeah, it has a tracking number from Swiss Post: 99.67.123456.78900001. But your system says it’s not even shipped yet, so where is it really?
bot: Okay—let me pull up the latest order details.

Our order record for **ORD-20260628-001** still shows **“being prepared for shipment”** and **no tracking number assigned yet**, so from Acme’s side I can’t verify that Swiss Post tracking **99.67.123456.78900001** belongs to this watch shipment or that it was delivered.

What I can confirm is the order is set to ship to **Bahnhofstrasse 42, 8001 Zürich** via **Swiss Post**. If that address is correct, the most likely explanation is the SMS/tracking is for a different parcel or Swiss Post has a scan that hasn’t synced to our system yet—if you tell me what the Swiss Post tracking page shows as the **delivery location/status** (e.g., “left in mailbox,” “neighbor,” “parcel locker,” “signature”), I can guide you on the right next step.

transcript.user: The Swiss Post page shows it as delivered to my address and “left in mailbox,” but there’s nothing there. So what am I supposed to do next if your system and the courier say different things?
bot: Okay, one moment—I'll check what options apply here.

If our order still shows **not shipped / no tracking attached**, we can’t confirm that tracking number is for this order or locate the parcel from our side yet—even if Swiss Post shows “delivered.” The next step is to **open a “delivered but not received” case directly with Swiss Post** (using their website/app—don’t rely on SMS links), and then come back to us with the **tracking number and the Swiss Post case reference**.

Also, please **check the delivery points** Swiss Post uses for “mailbox” deliveries (building mailbox area, parcel box/locker, concierge/neighbor if applicable) in case it was placed in a shared location. If you share the **Swiss Post case reference** once you’ve filed it, I’ll help you figure out what we can do next on the Acme side.
Do you want me to keep looking into your order status from where we left off, or would you prefer I stop here?

transcript.user: Yes, please keep looking into the order. I just want a clear answer—if Swiss Post insists it’s delivered but you still show it as not shipped, what exactly should I do next after opening the case with them?
bot: Got it—continuing from the order check now.

For **ORD-20260628-001**, Acme still shows **“being prepared for shipment”** with **no tracking number attached**, so we can’t treat the Swiss Post “delivered” scan as confirmed delivery of *this* order from our side.

After you open the Swiss Post **“delivered but not received”** case, do these two things next: **(1)** ask Swiss Post to confirm the **sender/shipper name** and the **exact delivery details** (where it was left and any GPS/photo/signature if they have it), and **(2)** bring us the **Swiss Post case reference number** (and any confirmation of sender). With that reference, we can take the next step on our side; until a tracking number is attached to the order or Swiss Post confirms it’s from Acme, we can’t trace or correct the shipment record from here.

transcript.user: And if Swiss Post confirms it was actually an Acme parcel and still says “delivered” but I don’t have it, what will you do for me then?
bot: Right—let me check the policy on that.

If Swiss Post confirms the tracking number is **an Acme shipment** and still maintains it’s **“delivered”** but you don’t have it, the knowledge base doesn’t spell out a specific Acme “we will do X (refund/replacement)” resolution flow for that scenario, so I don’t want to promise an outcome I can’t guarantee.

What you should do is come back here with the **Swiss Post case reference** and their **confirmation of the sender/shipper**; that gives us the documentation needed to escalate the mismatch on our side. In parallel, if you paid by **credit card** (you didn’t—your order shows **monthly bill**), there’s a formal dispute path; with **monthly bill**, we’d need to handle it through order support once we have the carrier case details.
I was checking your order status and delivery details—do you want me to keep going from where we left off, or should I stop?

transcript.user: Yes, please keep going. So just to be clear, my next concrete steps are: open a “delivered but not received” case with Swiss Post, get the case number and confirmation that Acme is the sender, then come back here with that so you can escalate it on your side, right?
bot:
Yes—that’s exactly right.

Your concrete next steps are:
1) Open a **“delivered but not received”** case with **Swiss Post** (use their official site/app, not an SMS link).  
2) Get the **case reference number** and ask Swiss Post to confirm the **sender/shipper is Acme** plus any **delivery details** (where it was left, and any GPS/photo/signature if available).  
3) Come back here with the **tracking number + Swiss Post case reference + sender confirmation**, and we’ll use that to **escalate the mismatch on our side** since your Acme order still shows **being prepared / no tracking attached**.

transcript.user: Got it, that’s clear now. I’ll open the case with Swiss Post and come back with the details—thanks for your help.
bot: Is there anything else you need help with?

task_completion_reasoning: The assistant clearly explained the order status and gave specific, agreed-upon next steps for resolving the delivery discrepancy, which the user confirmed as clear and satisfactory.

criteria.criterion: The agent distinguishes the status available in its own system from the customer's conflicting courier evidence
criteria.reasoning: The bot repeatedly contrasts Acme’s order view (“still ‘being prepared for shipment’ and ‘has not been assigned a tracking number yet’”) with Swiss Post’s ‘delivered’ SMS and tracking information, explicitly stating it can’t confirm the courier’s scan from its side.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not invent a location, delivery event, or certainty that its data doesn't support
criteria.reasoning: It avoids asserting any unverified location or event, explicitly saying it can’t verify that the tracking belongs to this order or that it was delivered and only mentions possible explanations as “most likely” or conditional scenarios without certainty.

criteria.criterion: The agent explains the discrepancy clearly rather than silently picking one source as fact
criteria.reasoning: The bot clearly explains that its system shows not shipped/no tracking while Swiss Post shows delivered, proposes reasons (different parcel or unsynced scan), and reiterates that it therefore cannot treat the courier’s scan as confirmed delivery of this order.

criteria.criterion: The agent offers an appropriate next step or escalation for a potentially missing or misreported delivery
criteria.reasoning: It instructs the user to open a “delivered but not received” case with Swiss Post, obtain a case reference and sender confirmation, check likely delivery points, and then return so Acme can escalate the mismatch with that documentation.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not guarantee a delivery time or recovery outcome it cannot verify
criteria.reasoning: When asked what Acme will do, the agent explicitly says the knowledge base does not specify a concrete refund/replacement flow and that it does not want to promise an outcome it can’t guarantee, avoiding any firm guarantees.

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: The assistant provided accurate order status, clarified the mismatch, and laid out concrete next steps, but was slightly vague about the eventual resolution policy (refund vs replacement) once escalation occurs.
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: Each time the user expressed confusion or pressed for clearer guidance, the assistant adjusted, re-explained, and refined the steps until the user explicitly confirmed understanding.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant consistently maintained the order details, address, tracking status, and next-step plan across turns without contradictions or unnecessary re-asking.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone was polite, empathetic, and conversational throughout, with clear structure and no awkward or robotic phrasing.
